newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani caretaker government may levy new taxes.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani caretaker government may levy new taxes.

text.p: Pakistan's government might have to levy new taxes to avert an economic crisis, caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid was quoted as saying on Saturday.

"It's not necessary that the fresh tax package would carry imposition of new taxes worth 25 billion rupees (about $625 million)...but the economic crisis still exists and to avert it we cannot avert further taxation," the official Associated Press of Pakistan (APP) news agency quoted him as saying in the Punjab province town of Multan.
Khalid did not indicate which sectors might bear the weight of any new taxes or other revenue-raising instruments.

But the independent newspaper Dawn said on Saturday that a meeting of the Economic Coordination Committee of Khalid's cabinet set for Sunday appeared set to approve an increase in the rates of natural gas ranging between 15 and 25 percent for domestic, commercial and industial consumers.

Pakistan, seeking the disbursement of stalled tranches from a $600 million standby loan from the International Monetary Fund, is trying to contain its budget deficit to four percent in fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) from an estimated 6.3 percent of the gross domestic product in 1995/96, reduce domestic bank borrowing and boost sagging foreign exchange reserves.
